subject: MSA & Order Form — security exhibit redlines and evidence cadence
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthstream.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@healthstream.com; kevin.oneill@healthstream.com
Date: Tue, 03 Jun 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Security exhibit questions + quick follow on pen test language

Vanessa / Laura —

Thanks for the redlined MSA and Order Form. We reviewed the security exhibit (v3) and have three open items before we can route to legal/procurement:

1) SOC 2 report cadence — the redline currently lists annual attestation with evidence by request. Our InfoSec team prefers the ability to receive a copy of the SOC 2 + a quarterly evidence digest for service changes. Can you confirm cadence and whether a digest is possible?

2) Penetration testing — we need clarity on scope: are third-party infra scans included (cloud provider surfaces) or limited to application-layer testing? Also want to understand notice windows and a defined remediation SLA for high/critical findings.

3) Audit access — the exhibit says "reasonable access"; procurement is pushing for a clearer timeframe for scheduled inspections (e.g., 2 weeks notice and max 1 week on-site window). Is that something Redwood is open to?

I've attached our internal risk summary for reference (see attachment: HealthStream_Risk_Summary.pdf). Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow if easier.

Thanks —
Elena Morales
Director, Information Risk
HealthStream
elena.morales@healthstream.com
(615) 555-0123

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Security exhibit questions + quick follow on pen test language

Elena —

Appreciate the clear notes and the risk summary. We're happy to align on these items; looping in Laura (security) and Connor (legal) to scope a concise response and propose text.

Quick answers while the team drafts:
- SOC 2: Redwood conducts annual SOC 2 Type II; we can provide the report upon NDA + offer a quarterly operational digest that highlights material platform changes and control updates.
- Pen test scope: typical scope includes Redwood-managed application and orchestration layers; cloud provider infrastructure scans (host-level) are generally out of scope unless explicitly included in the Order Form. We can propose a carveout/extension for provider-scoped testing if HealthStream requires it, with associated scheduling constraints.
- Audit access: we can agree to scheduled inspections with 2 weeks notice and propose a 5-business-day on-site window; need legal sign-off for exceptions.

I'll put together a clean redline and a short proposal for wording for each item (SOC 2 digest template + pen test SOW attachment + audit window language) and share in the next 24 hours. Would you prefer a doc or a brief call?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Security exhibit questions + quick follow on pen test language

Team —

Forwarding HealthStream's asks (below). Key asks to address in our redline + short rationale document:

A) SOC 2 cadence + quarterly digest: propose we offer a SOC 2 Type II report on NDA and a quarterly digest that summarizes control/ops changes (no raw artifacts). Need legal language that limits use and prohibits redistribution.

B) Pen test scope & remediation SLA: suggest we keep cloud provider hosts out of scope by default, but offer an optional expanded SOW for provider-scoped testing (one-time add-on). For remediation SLA: propose 30 calendar days for critical findings with immediate mitigation steps documented; 90 days for medium/low. Legal — confirm whether Redwood is comfortable with fixed SLAs vs. "reasonable efforts".

C) Audit access windows: propose acceptance of scheduled inspections with 10 business days' notice and a 5-business-day access window (we may need to carve out live-prod-ops blackout periods). Also propose remote evidence-first approach (SOC2 + logs) before on-site.

Action items I want from you:
- Karthik: draft redline text for pen test SOW add-on and remediation commitments (paperwork + liability limitations).
- Connor: propose specific audit-window wording and use limitations for SOC 2 digest distribution.
- Laura: review proposed security language and confirm whether quarterly digest content is safe to share.

HealthStream is asking for timeline; they'd like to close commercial terms next week if possible. Can we get first draft redline + rationale by EOD today so I can send to Elena tomorrow morning?

Thanks —
Vanessa

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai; laura_bennett@redwood.ai; connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Morales <elena.morales@healthstream.com>; Kevin O'Neill <kevin.oneill@healthstream.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security exhibit questions + quick follow on pen test language

Vanessa / team / Elena / Kevin —

Thanks for the context and HealthStream's asks. Attached are the proposed redline excerpts and a short playbook explaining the tradeoffs. High-level summary below and next steps.

1) SOC 2 + quarterly digest: redline language accepts delivery of SOC 2 Type II upon execution of an NDA. We offer a quarterly "operational digest" that includes high-level change notes (date, component, control affected) and whether the change had material impact to assertions. The digest will never include raw logs or PII. Proposed clause includes a strict redistribution prohibition and a requirement that HealthStream limit circulation to named stakeholders.

2) Pen test SOW (attachment: PenTest-SOW.xlsx): default scope remains Redwood-managed application stack. If HealthStream requires cloud provider scope, we will add an optional SOW addendum with explicit testing windows, coordination with provider, and liability carveouts. Remediation SLA is set as follows in the redline:
- Critical: initial remediation plan within 48 hours; final remediation within 30 calendar days.
- High: remediation within 60 calendar days.
- Medium/Low: remediation within 90 calendar days.
We modeled SLAs as commitments to deliverables and documented exceptions for third-party dependencies. Please note liability caps remain as per MSA, and we do not accept unlimited liability for third-party infrastructure.

3) Audit access: redline accepts scheduled inspections with 10 business days' notice and a 5-business-day inspection window. We added a clause prioritizing remote evidence (SOC2, audit logs, redacted config snapshots) before on-site activities. Any on-site access will be scoped to pre-agreed environments and must avoid blackout windows tied to major releases.

Attachments: Security_Exhibit_v3_redline.pdf (redline), PenTest-SOW.xlsx (SOW), SOC2-report-2024.pdf (sample report)

Next steps: Vanessa to send the redline packet to HealthStream with a 30-min call option for walk-through. If HealthStream confirms cloud-provider testing requirement, we will price the SOW add-on and return a commercial amendment.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
